chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd narrated from Sulaymān ibn Ḥafṣ al-Marwazī, who said:

I wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام concerning a man who died while owing a debt and left nothing except a pledged item in the possession of one of them, and its price did not amount to more than the property-right of the pledge-holder. May he take it for his claim, or are he and the rest of the creditors partners in it?
So he عليه السلام wrote: “All the creditors in that are equal; they distribute it among themselves according to their shares.”
He said: And I wrote to him concerning a man who died and had heirs, then a man came and claimed that the deceased owed him property and that he had a pledge in his possession.

So he عليه السلام wrote: “If he has property due from the deceased and has no evidence for it against him, then let him take his property from what is in his hand and return the remainder to his heirs. And whenever he acknowledges what is in his possession, he is held to it and is required to produce evidence for his claim, and his right is fulfilled after the oath. And whenever he does not establish evidence and the heirs are denying, then he has against them an oath of knowledge: they swear by Allah that they do not know that he has any right against their deceased.”

key_terms.الدُّيَّانِ: the creditors who are owed claims
key_terms.الْمُرْتَهِنِ: the pledge-holder or creditor in possession of the collateral
key_terms.بَيِّنَةَ: legal evidence or proof for a claim
key_terms.بِالْحِصَصِ: in proportion to their respective shares or claims
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: a debt owed by the deceased
key_terms.رَهْنًا: a pledged item held as security for a claim
key_terms.يَمِينُ عِلْمٍ: an oath based on one's knowledge, swearing lack of knowledge of the claim

ai.seo_question: How is pledged property handled when a debtor dies owing money, and what if a claimant has no evidence against the deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning pledged property, debts of the deceased, and the rights of heirs and creditors. It establishes that creditors share proportionally in pledged assets and clarifies procedure when a claimant lacks evidence, including possession, proof, and the heirs’ oath of knowledge.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4111 - Muhammad bin Isa bin Ubaid narrated from Sulaiman bin Hafs Al-Marwazi, who said:

I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (as) about a man who died and had a debt, leaving nothing except a pledged item in the possession of someone. The value of the pledge did not exceed the creditor's due amount. I asked whether the creditor could take it for his claim or if all creditors shared in it.
Imam (as) wrote: "All creditors are equal in this matter and must distribute it among themselves in proportion to their claims."
He further said: I wrote to Imam (as) about a man who died, leaving heirs. Then someone came forward, claiming a debt against him and that he held a pledge for it.

Imam (as) wrote: "If he has a claim against the deceased but has no evidence for it, he may take his due from what is in his possession and return the remainder to the heirs. However, if he admits to what he possesses, he is bound by it and must provide evidence for his claim. He must fulfill his right after swearing an oath. If he cannot provide evidence and the heirs deny the claim, then the heirs must take an oath of knowledge, swearing by Allah (swt) that they have no knowledge of any right owed to him by their deceased."
